title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-kai-martinez
content:
Objective: quick scratchpad on recurrent GPU OOMs and driver/library mismatch errors seen on gpu-node-14. Collect commands, errors, hypotheses, and next steps. Informal notes — messy.

Environment snapshot:
- Host: gpu-node-14 (prod-ish, shared with batch jobs)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- NVIDIA driver: 525.85.12 (reported by apt), nvidia-smi shows 525.116.03 (suspicious mismatch)
- CUDA toolkit on host: /usr/local/cuda-11.8 (symlink points to cuda-11.8)
- Container base: ubuntu:20.04 + python3.10
- PyTorch (inside container): torch==2.2.0+cu118 (pip wheel), torchvision==0.15.2
- Runtime: Docker 24.0 + nvidia-container-toolkit 2.12

Commands run and outputs (raw-ish):
- nvidia-smi
  Tue Feb 24 10:12:03 2026
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 525.116.03    Driver Version: 525.116.03    CUDA Version: 12.0 |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  NOTE: CUDA Version reported by nvidia-smi is 12.0, but toolkit is 11.8 on host.

- docker run --gpus all --rm -it image:gpu-test bash -c "python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())'"
  -> prints: 11.8
  -> torch.cuda.is_available() == True

Symptom logs from failing job (ML training):
- RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 28.12 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 26.34 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
- Afterwards container exits with code 134 (abort).

Other errors seen intermittently on this node:
- E/torcher: failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch
- RuntimeError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
- ImportError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory (happened when someone built container against cuda11.0 libs)
- WARN: GPU watchdog timeout detected (killed long kernel)

Debug steps tried so far (chronological):
1) Confirm driver/toolkit mismatch: ran dpkg -l | grep -i nvidia; found packages from different installs. Suspect partial apt + runfile driver installs mixed in.
2) Rebooted node (cheap step) — freed up leaked memory temporarily, OOM recurred after several hours under load.
3) ldd on container libtorch.so shows it links to libcudart.so.11.8 which exists in the image. But host nvidia libs (via driver) advertise CUDA 12.0 in nvidia-smi -> potential ABI mismatch but usually backwards-compatible.
4) Ran dmesg | grep -i nvidia -> saw repeated: NVIDIA: failed to load: libnvidia-ml.so.1: version `NVIDIA_...` not found -> evidence of mixed driver versions.
5) Tried torch.cuda.empty_cache() and manual del(tensor) in training loop — temporary relief but not root cause.
6) Lowered batch size from 64->32 -> stops OOMs for same experiment but only increases latency.
7) Tried setting environment TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 -> reduced fragmentation OOMs in some runs.
8) Rebuilt container referencing cuda toolkit 12.0 libs -> some jobs then failed with "No kernel image is available for execution on the device" on older GPUs (P4/P40) -> indicates GPU compute capability mismatch when building with newer CUDA arch flags.

Hypotheses / likely causes:
- Host drivers are inconsistent (some driver components at 525.116.03, others left at 525.85.12) due to mixed install methods -> intermittent NVML/library mismatches. Could cause NVML init failures and unpredictable behavior.
- CUDA toolkit vs driver reported version mismatch: nvidia-smi -> CUDA 12.0 but containers built against cuda11.8. Generally compatible, but edge cases (kernel driver ABI changes) can lead to unspecified launch failures.
- Memory fragmentation / persistent allocations by other processes on the node; shared cluster setup means leftover memory from other users can cause high reserved memory.
- Driver bug causing leaks over time (observed OOM after many hours even with same workload that used to be stable).
- Some containers built against wrong libcuda/libcudart versions (11.0 vs 11.8 vs 12.0) causing immediate import errors.

Repro steps to isolate (next):
- Reproduce in a fresh node (freshly rebooted, no other processes) using the failing image and the failing workload to confirm if issue is workload-only or node-contamination.
- Run stress test: tiny training loop that allocates >90% GPU mem and then frees repeatedly to trigger fragmentation quickly. Measure when OOM triggers.
- Run a simple CUDA sample (vectorAdd) compiled for 11.8 and 12.0 to check ABI/compatibility.
- Use nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY every 30s to log usage from all processes; correlate with OOM time.

Immediate mitigation actions suggested:
- For production: pin models to smaller batch sizes / enable gradient checkpointing / mixed precision (AMP) to lower peak mem.
- Set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 in environments with fragmentation complaints.
- Temporarily cordon the node (drain) for debugging if OOMs are impacting customers.
- Ensure a consistent method for driver installs across fleet (prefer apt packages matching distro + nvidia repo). Audit /var/log/apt/history.log and /var/log/installer.

Longer-term fixes / ops items:
- Schedule one maintenance window: fully purge drivers and do a clean apt install of NVIDIA driver 525.* matching the team standard (document exact package names). Reboot and run smoke tests.
- Add node-level startup checks: run ldd /usr/bin/nvidia-smi? or a small script that verifies libcuda version coherence and fails healthcheck if mixed versions detected.
- Improve container policy: standardize base images on specific cuXX + matching driver compatibility matrix; block builds that link to nonexistent libcuda versions.
- Add periodic nvml/driver sanity checks to SRE monitors (nvmlInit result, nvidia-smi CUDA version vs expected).

Notes / small snippets to save:
- How to check for mixed installs:
  dpkg -l | grep -i nvidia
  lsmod | grep nvidia
  readlink -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1
  apt-cache policy nvidia-driver-525

- Quick libcudart lookup in container:
  docker run --rm image:gpu-test bash -c "python - <<'PY'
import ctypes, os
try:
  ctypes.CDLL('libcudart.so')
  print('libcudart found')
except Exception as e:
  print('libcudart missing', e)
print(os.listdir('/usr/local'))
PY"

- If NVML errors: check /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and dmesg for "NVRM: Xid" errors. Xid codes are helpful (e.g., Xid 31 often indicates a GPU page fault or illegal instruction).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who ran a runfile installer on this node last month? Need to ask infra team — suspected due to apt+runfile mix.
- Repro on a clean node (I will try on gpu-node-20 tomorrow AM).
- Validate whether mixed driver versions can cause "unspecified launch failure" or if that's purely kernel/compute mismatch. Might need to open a ticket with NVIDIA if we can reproduce consistently.

Reference links (internal):
- Confluence memory OOM runbook: /display/SERV/Memory+OOM+Runbook
- Nvidia driver install best practices: https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/tesla/tesla-installation-notes/index.html

Bottom line: likely a mix of driver/install mismatch + memory fragmentation and occasional heavier workloads. Priority: cordon node + audit drivers, reproduce on fresh host, then decide between driver reinstall vs container rebuilds.

-- Kai
